text:
sarah: Heads-up — after the RBAC merge at 11:12 we started seeing a subset of mTLS connections from multi-tenant ingress get rejected.

morgan: Saw the same. Affected tenants: acct-prod-42 and acct-prod-77. Failures hit the acceptor layer (ingress-proxy).

anita: Logs show `handshake error: no certificate for SNI`. I pulled the proxy logs:

sarah: ```
ingress-proxy@acceptor0 ERROR: tls: client hello for 'acct-prod-42' -> no matching cert in store
ingress-proxy@acceptor0 DEBUG: cert-mapping lookup for sni='acct-prod-42' returned nil
kms-unseal@worker INFO: decrypt request for key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/tenant-certs/cryptoKeys/ingress-cert (ok)
```

morgan: The RBAC change restricted the proxy service account's access to the tenant-certs KMS key. Audit shows a deny on `kms.decrypt` for `svc/ingress-proxy` after the merge (commit d4b2f6).

anita: Confirmed in audit logs: `principal=svc/ingress-proxy action=kms.decrypt status=DENIED reason=iam.policy#deny` at 11:12:17. So proxy couldn't decrypt per-tenant cert bundles; mapping returned empty -> handshake rejects.

kim: Ugh. That would explain why only some tenants are impacted — the per-tenant certs are stored encrypted under separate KMS keys. Some tenants still matched a global fallback cert, others did not.

sarah: Immediate mitigation idea: re-grant decrypt to ingress-proxy for the ingress-cert key via the emergency allowlist role, or add a temporary fallback cert for affected SVCS while we fix RBAC. Opinions?

morgan: re-grant looks simplest. But we need an auditable path. Suggest: 1) create a short-lived policy binding for `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` scoped to the key and `svc/ingress-proxy`; 2) record the change in audit ticket; 3) roll forward a least-privilege fix.

anita: Agreed. Also putting a fallback cert in the proxy requires a restart on many nodes — higher blast radius. Prefer policy change first.

kim: I'll prepare the IAM patch. Quick Q: can we limit it to the exact key name? We need to avoid broad perms.

morgan: Yes scope to `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/tenant-certs/cryptoKeys/ingress-cert`. Add a condition if available: `request.time < timestamp("2026-03-23T12:00:00Z")` for auto-expiry.

anita: Nice. Also add the justification in the commit and link to the audit ticket: SEC-INC-2026-142.

devops-bot: detected deploy window 12:00-12:10 UTC. Please ack to proceed. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sarah: Ack on my side. kim, want to apply the change and share the policy diff in this thread? I'll watch metrics and tls-handshake success.

kim: Pushing policy now (will post diff).

kim: ```diff
- bindings: []
+ bindings:
+ - role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
+   members: ["serviceAccount:svc-ingress-proxy@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
+   condition: "request.time < \"2026-03-23T12:00:00Z\""
```

morgan: Once that's live, we should see decrypt successes in the KMS audit and cert-mapping fill for those tenants. I'll tail logs.

anita: After policy applied: KMS shows `status=OK` for decrypts at 11:13:02 and ingress-proxy logs now: `cert-mapping found bundle for acct-prod-42` — handshakes recovering.

sarah: Nice. Can we get a short postmortem planned? We need: root cause (RBAC merge included a deny rule), mitigation actions, timeline, long-term fix (update RBAC automation to whitelist critical service accounts or verify KMS perms in merge CI).

kim: I'll open SEC-PR-2026-142-PM and assign owners. Long-term options: add unit tests in PR pipeline to simulate decrypt calls, or a pre-merge policy simulator that rejects PRs which would remove `kms.decrypt` for service accounts in the ingress allowlist.

morgan: Also worth adding alarm on `kms.decrypt` DENIED spikes and a dashboard tile showing per-tenant handshake failure rate.

anita: +1. I'll draft detection rule: alert if `kms.decrypt` denied count > 5 in 1m for any ingress-proxy principal.

sarah: Thanks all — good catch. Leave notes in SEC-INC-2026-142 and mark this thread resolved once PM doc exists. :white_check_mark:
